title: Younger people liked bebop, his generation did not
summary: Scott has not changed his mind about modern jazz.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What about today, when you hear someone like Oscar Petersen? Is that too far out for you?
I don't know. When did you hear him last?

Probably, yeah. I'm just wondering -- I know that bebop when it first came out, it was kind of startling to a lot of people who were not used to it. But as the years have gone by, and this other music has appeared that sounds even farther out --
-- bebop begins to sound a little normal, doesn't it?
Yeah, well, see, it took to the younger people. They came up with bebop, yeah.
And they liked it more. But the fellows my age and all like that, they didn't like it. They didn't like it.
Well, have you changed your mind at all about bebop or modern jazz?
